question:
A 59-year-old female smoker (10 pack-year history) is receiving induction chemotherapy with
doxorubicin, methotrexate, and cyclophosphamide for estrogen and progesterone receptor-positive,
Her2-negative invasive ductal carcinoma of the left breast. Her treatment plan includes subsequent
radiation and hormonal therapy. Prior to treatment, her echocardiogram showed normal biventricular
function, and her blood work, including electrolytes and complete blood count, was within normal limits.
During the third day of chemotherapy, she develops persistent painless hematuria starting in the
morning. Which preventive measure could have reduced the likelihood of this complication? Answer
Choices: (A) Decreased methotrexate dose (B) Enhanced diuresis with loop diuretics (C) Avoidance of
cyclophosphamide (D) Reduction of chemotherapy infusion rate (E) Pre-treatment with glucocorticoids
(F) Mesna co-administration (G) Urine alkalinization (H) Urine antioxidation (I) Use of liposomal
doxorubicin (J) Aggressive hydration
 A. Urine antioxidation
B. Pre-treatment with glucocorticoids
C. Reduction of chemotherapy infusion rate
D. Mesna co-administration
E. Aggressive hydration
F. Avoidance of cyclophosphamide
G. Use of liposomal doxorubicin
H. Urine alkalinization
I. Decreased methotrexate dose
J. Enhanced diuresis with loop diuretics
